question: Is there an English major at Ramapo? What does it involve?
answer:
Yes. Ramapo offers an English and Literary Studies major, a Bachelor of Arts in the School of Arts, Humanities, and Education. [1] Students develop critical thinking, reading, research, oral communication, and writing skills through literary study. [5] The major describes literature as an aesthetic endeavor, cultural critique, and personal search; coursework, internships, cooperative education, and service learning can connect students with community and professional settings. [1][5]

The curriculum has several options, including Creative Writing and Specialized Studies concentrations and Teacher Education tracks. Requirements include LITR 203 Methods of Literary Study and LITR 414 Seminar, plus selections in areas such as critical approaches, diverse perspectives, early literature in English, global perspectives, and literature electives. Creative Writing adds LITR 280 Introduction to Creative Writing, LITR 381 Creative Writing Capstone, and workshops. The exact course choices vary by track; see the [catalog requirements](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/AH-BA-ENLS). [1]

The catalog describes career and graduate-study paths including publishing, government, business, law, science, journalism, diplomacy, public relations, higher education, and library sciences. [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/AH-BA-ENLS) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/study-abroad/academic-search/literature/)

question: what classes do i need to take for the psychology major and how many credits is it total
answer:
Psychology BA (Bachelor of Arts) requirements [1]:
• Required: PSYC 101 Introduction to Psychology; PSYC 242 Statistics; both PSYC 303 Research Methods in Psychology and PSYC 304 Data Analysis in Psychology.
• Choose 1 from each: Social/organizational—PSYC 226 Social Psychology, PSYC 345 Workplace Psychology; cognition/perception—PSYC 202 Psychology of Learning, PSYC 209 Psychology of Perception, PSYC 227 Cognitive Psychology; developmental—PSYC 212 Psychology of Aging, PSYC 241 Developmental Psychology, PSYC 263 Child Psychology, PSYC 347 Adolescent Psychology.
• Choose 1 from each: sociocultural—PSYC 231 Multicultural Psychology, PSYC 239 Cross-Cultural Psychology, PSYC 307 Psychology of Yoga, PSYC 311 Psychology of Gender, PSYC 335 Sexualities and Gender Identities: LGBTQA+, PSYC 349 Psychology of Women; clinical—PSYC 314 Psychopathology, PSYC 321 Theories of Personality, PSYC 357 Childhood Disorders; brain/behavior—PSYC 310 Neuropsychology, PSYC 352 Behavioral Neuroscience, PSYC 353 Cognitive Neuroscience, PSYC 355 Neuropsychopharmacology.
• Choose 1 fieldwork/research: PSYC 319, 320, 339, 358, 367, 368 or 472; and 1 capstone: PSYC 430–434, 436–440, 450 or 451. Also select 1 additional Psychology course (no options specified). Career Pathways requires PATH 001 (listed twice) and PATH 003. [1]
The recommended 2026–2027 plan totals 128 credits for the degree, not just the major. [1] The pages do not give an exact Psychology-major credit total; the catalog says undergraduate major requirements must be at least 40 and no more than 64 credits. [3] Also published: Psychology Minor. [1]

question: I'm a parent looking at the social work program for my daughter. What are the degree requirements and does it include any field placement or internship?
answer:
The Social Work BSW is a Bachelor of Social Work; the College also publishes a Social Work MSW. [1]

Requirements shown: Science Requirement—Required Course (the listing names no course). Social Work Program Required Courses: PSYC 101 INTRODUCTION TO PSYCHOLOGY; one of SOCI 101 INTRODUCTION TO SOCIOLOGY, SOCI 205 SOCIOLOGY OF AGING, or SOCI 232 SOCIOLOGY OF FAMILY; one of SWRK 202 POLITICAL ECONOMY OF SOCIAL WELFARE or ECON 102 INTRODUCTION TO MACROECONOMICS; SWRK 222 HISTORY AND PHILOSOPHY OF SOCIAL WELFARE; SWRK 225 INTRODUCTION TO SOCIAL WORK; SWRK 270 CULTURAL DIVERSITY: RACISM, OPPRESSION AND PRIVILEGE; SWRK 307 SOCIAL WORK RESEARCH METHODS; SWRK 329 SOCIAL WORK IN AGENCIES AND COMMUNITIES; SWRK 362 HUMAN BEHAVIOR AND THE SOCIAL ENVIRONMENT I - THEORIES OF HUMAN DEVELOPMENT; SWRK 363 HUMAN BEHAVIOR AND THE SOCIAL ENVIRONMENT II - LIFE CYCLE; SWRK 420 CONTEMPORARY SOCIAL POLICY; SWRK 425 SOCIAL WORK THEORY AND PRACTICE I; and SWRK 426 SOCIAL WORK THEORY & PRACTICE II. Career Pathways: PATH 001, PATH 002, and PATH 003 (CAREER PATHWAYS MOD 1, 2, and 3). [1]

The recommended plan applies to students admitted to the major in 2026-2027. Each semester is 16 credits: First Year Fall and Spring; Second Year Fall and Spring; Third Year Fall and Spring; Fourth Year Fall and Spring. Total Credits Required: 128 credits; GPA: 2.75. [1]

Yes. The plan includes SWRK 329 with 100 hours of fieldwork (must be accepted into the major before taking it); SWRK 425 with 200 hours in fieldwork (SWRK 329 is a prerequisite); and SWRK 426 with 200 hours in fieldwork (SWRK 425 is a prerequisite). It does not identify these as internships. [1]

question: What does psych 101 cover and is it a prerequisite for other psych classes?
answer:
PSYC 101, “Introduction to Psychology,” is a 4-credit introduction to psychology as a field of study and practice. It explores the history, methods, and scope of psychology, including learning, perception, cognition, emotion, motivation, abnormal behavior, psychotherapy, social behavior, personality, development across the lifespan, and the biological bases of thought, feeling, and action. [1]

The catalog lists no prerequisites for PSYC 101. [1] It does not say whether PSYC 101 is a prerequisite for other psychology courses. To check a specific class, select Psychology on the course-prerequisites page and review the requirements in Web Self Service. [2][3][4]

question: does Ramapo offer a masters in education? what are the courses like
answer:
Yes. Ramapo lists the Master of Arts in Special Education (MASE) and Master of Science in Educational Technology (MSET). [5][6] The MASE is a 36-credit, in-seat cohort program focused on individualized, student-focused learning and preparation for Teacher of Students with Disabilities Certification; it starts in fall only. [4]

The MASE curriculum balances theory and practice, with experiential learning and instructional strategies. [1] Its required courses are: EDSP 610 Home School and Community for Diverse Learners; EDSP 615 Language, Literacy and Learning in a Diverse Setting; EDSP 620 Implementation of Professional Skills (Field Component); EDSP 625 School Based Assessment and Implementing Data Driven; EDSP 630 Interdisciplinary Studies in a Diverse Classroom; EDSP 635 Inclusion; EDSP 640 Assistive Technology; EDSP 705 Thesis Seminar; EDSP 720 Capstone Research Project I; and EDSP 725 Capstone Research Project II. [1]

The MSET is a 34-credit hybrid program for teachers or professionals who want to integrate technology into classrooms and address diverse learning styles and performance levels. It has fall, spring, and summer start options. [6]

For more information, contact Graduate Admissions: graduate@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7270. [4][5][6]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/AH-MA-MASE) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/home/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/home/)

question: What are the general education requirements for all students? I'm trying to figure out how many gen ed classes I would have to take outside my major if I did communication arts.
answer:
Ramapo’s general education curriculum is ten courses: four keystone courses, one in each of four keystone categories, and one course in two of three distribution categories. [3]
1. Keystone courses: First Year Seminar, Social Science Inquiry, Critical Reading & Writing 102 (within the first 64 credits), and Studies in the Arts & Humanities. [3]
2. Keystone categories: one course each in Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Scientific Reasoning, and Quantitative Reasoning (within the first 64 credits). [3]
3. Distribution: one course in two of Culture & Creativity, Systems, Sustainability, & Society, and Values & Ethics. At least one course must be offered by a school other than the one housing your major. [3]
The catalog also lists Critical Reading and Writing II, Historical Perspectives, Scientific Reasoning, and Global Awareness, plus two distribution categories. [4] Section 6 says that starting Fall 2026, the “out of school requirement” is no longer enforced in degree audit tools; section 3 says at least one distribution course must be offered by another school. The pages differ on that rule. [3][6]
For Communication Arts BA, the 2026–2027 recommended plan places General Education Requirement courses in several semesters, but does not specify how many gen ed classes must be taken outside the major. [1] The catalog says no more than two General Education courses may double count in both Gen Ed and the major. [5] The plan lists General Education categories and some major courses mapped to them; it is a recommended plan for students admitted during 2026–2027. [1]
For advising about which requirements remain, contact the Center for Student Success (Academic Advising): success@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7441. [2]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/AH-BA-COMM) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#waiver-of-general-education-requirements1) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#general-education) [5](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/home/comprehensive-academic-plan/resources/)

- First Year*, Spring (total 16 credits): QUANTITATIVE REASONING – MATH 108 - ELEMENTARY PROBABILITY AND STATISTICS {recommended} (4); General Education Requirement (4); PSYC 215 - LEARNING, COGNITION, AND TEACHING (4); EDUC 211 - STUDENT LITERACY CORPS CE1 (Urban) (4); PATH 001 - CAREER PATHWAYS MOD 1. [1]
- Second Year**, Fall (total 16 credits): General Education Requirement (4); VALUES AND ETHICS – EDUC 221 - SOCIAL CONTEXT OF EDUCATION (4); General Education Requirement (4); SCIENTIFIC REASONING – BIOL 101 - INTRODUCTION TO BIOLOGY (recommended) (4); PATH 002 - CAREER PATHWAYS MOD 2. [1]
- Second Year**, Spring (total 16 credits): EDUC 222 - TEACHING: PRINCIPLES AND PRACTICES CE2 (Note: Must Be Fully Admitted to Teacher Education Program) (4); choose one: LITR 302 - GRAMMAR: THEORY AND PEDAGOGY or LITR 203 - METHODS OF LITERARY STUDY (HRS 4) or LITR 306 - LITERARY THEORY (HRS 4) (4); two Electives (Middle School Content for those interested) (4 each); PATH 003 - CAREER PATHWAYS MOD 3; EDUC 241 - INSTRUCTIONAL TECHNOLOGY (4). [1]
- Third Year, Fall (total 16 credits): Elective (Middle School Content for those interested) (4); Elective (PSYC 347 - ADOLESCENT PSYCHOLOGY) (for those interested in Middle School) (4); EDUC 360 - INTRODUCTION TO SPECIAL EDUCATION CE3*** with EDUC 301 - MEETING THE NEEDS OF ALL LEARNERS (co-req.) (4); choose one: LITR 308 - CHILDREN'S AND YOUNG ADULT LITERATURE or LITR 290 - TOPICS: (Permission Required) (DC for Culture/Creativity) (HRS 4) or LITR 279 - THE GRAPHIC NOVEL (HRS 4) (4). [1]
- Third Year, Spring (total 16 credits): General Education Requirement (4); MATH 210 - MATHEMATICS FOR ELEMENTARY EDUCATORS (4); SCIN 215 - SCIENCE FOR ELEMENTARY EDUCATORS (4); EDUC 346 - LITERACY THEORY & PRACTICE CE4 (Must have copy of substitute teacher license in TED account PRIOR to meeting with advisor) (4). [1]
- Fourth Year*****, Fall (total 16 credits): EDUC 370 - METHODS OF TEACHING ELEMENTARY MATHEMATICS CP1**** (4); EDUC 375 - METHODS OF TEACHING ELEMENTARY SCIENCE CP2**** (4); EDUC 365 - LITERACY ACROSS THE ELEMENTARY CURRICULUM CP3**** (4); EDUC 390 - TOPICS: CP4**** (4). [1]

question: Can I double major in political science and law and society, and is there a minor in either one?
answer:
